alignments.note: The ASV writes no word for δέ here (rule 23's shape for a connective).
Substantival article supplying the nominal 'own', the possessive being already taken (rules 20, 22).

Corrected. This article governs the elided head noun (συνείδησιν), and the English prenominal possessive 'the other's' occupies its determiner slot, so it realizes nothing under rule 20, exactly as a genitive noun rendered with 's empties the article of τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας → 'Caesar's household'. It kept 'the' before; that 'the' determines 'other' and is the inner article's, as 10:24's 'his' is. Where the ASV supplies a nominal for this slot the article takes it under rule 102, which is why 10:24's τό keeps 'good' and 10:33's τό keeps 'the profit'; here the ASV supplies none.

Corrected. The inner article takes the determiner the ASV writes on the possessor phrase, under rule 19, as it takes 'his' in 10:24's 'his neighbor's good' for the identical τοῦ ἑτέρου — the ASV's own note there glosses the Greek 'the other's', which is what stands here. Reading 'the' as the outer article's determiner is the competing analysis and was taken before; it fails because a possessive phrase's determiner determines the possessor, and rule 20 has already emptied the article that possessive displaced.
The genitive μου is free and takes 'my', so the article realizes nothing (rule 20).
Passive verb with its copula, discontinuous (rule 15); head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: Corrected the doubled article of ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑτέρου: the outer τήν (s008) is now unrepresented under rule 20 and the inner τοῦ (s009) takes the 'the' that the English possessive writes on its possessor, as 10:24 gives 'his' to the inner τοῦ of 'his neighbor's good' for the same Greek.
Nothing else in the verse changed; τήν/ἑαυτοῦ still reads as at 10:24 and 10:33, the reflexive taking the possessive and the article the supplied nominal 'own' (rules 20, 22).
All 19 source and 18 target ids partitioned exactly once.
